Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
747 PM EDT Thu Aug 6 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 229 PM EDT Thursday...

No significant changes we made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 229 PM EDT Thursday...

1. A Bermuda high pattern will set up today through the 
weekend, which will bring warm, humid conditions and daily chances 
for showers and thunderstorms. A few will be capable of locally 
heavy rain.

2. Cooler temperatures are expected next week with a couple 
chances for additional showers.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 229 PM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A Bermuda high will develop off the coast of the SE 
CONUS leading to anticyclonic flow to our south, aiding in the 
advection of increasing moisture and warmer air. Broad cyclonic 
flow, north of the Bermuda high, over our region, in association 
with increasing warm and moist air, will lead to several shortwaves 
each day through the weekend. While there is not a real defined 
boundary, diurnally driven instability in tandem with a modest 
shortwave is supporting scattered showers and thunderstorms 
currently over the Adirondacks. Mesoanalysis denotes terrain 
instability around 1000-1500J/kg with around 20-30 knots of shear 
early this afternoon, though mid level lapse rates appear to be 
modest at best around 5-6C/km. With light southwesterly flow, some 
of these showers will drift east into the Champlain Valley by early 
to mid this afternoon. Should ingredients align, there is a chance 
for some stronger storms, mainly over the Adirondacks, with lesser 
chances in the central Champlain Valley. As opposed to previous 
forecasts, the probability of any wet microbursts looks to have 
weakened with the axis of better DCAPE west of the instability axis. 
Nonetheless, a sub severe stronger gust may be possible as cells 
decay. The main impacts today will be the chance for locally heavy 
rain. Good moisture advection with PWs approaching 2" will lead to 
some heavy downpours under any showers today. Showers are expected 
to wane by sunset with the loss of diurnal heating. Temperatures 
will remain elevated with lingering moist conditions. It will still 
feel muggy with temperatures only lowering to the upper 60s to low 
70s, and dewpoints still in the upper 60s to low 70s as well. A few 
high min temperature records may be approached or broken tonight as 
a result, particularly at PBG. With ambient low level moisture, 
regardless of cloud cover, patchy fog may be possible in the usual 
river valleys, and could even drift into the unfavored locations, 
should an area receive showers this afternoon. 

By Friday, southwesterly flow and shear will increase to 30-40 knots 
with similar instability levels, expanding into the northern 
Champlain Valley as well. Afternoon scattered showers and 
thunderstorms are anticipated, mainly over the terrain. Shower 
coverage will be less than today with reduced chances for any 
stronger storms due to the lack of a defined trough. Any storms will 
also wane with the loss of diurnal heating in the evenings. Saturday 
looks to be the best chance areawide for any showers and 
thunderstorms. Widespread instability with a more defined trough are 
expected. Temperature wise, highs will get a degree or two cooler 
each day as the Bermuda High slowly sinks south as troughing becomes 
more dominate towards the end of the weekend.

KEY MESSAGE 2: As Bermuda high weakens and westerly flows prevails 
across the region, will see a cooling temperature trend next week. 
Highs at the start of the week will be in the upper 70s to mid 80s, 
but by the middle of the week they will drop a few degrees to be in 
the lower 70s and low 80s. A couple fronts will move through the 
region bringing widespread showers and a few possible thunderstorms, 
although the timing of the boundaries will have a large influence on 
any convective elements.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 00Z Saturday...Ongoing scattered showers, and a couple 
of thunderstorms currently in the Champlain Valley, are moving 
towards the east and should diminish gradually over the next 
couple of hours. No direct hits are expected based on radar 
trends, but a vicinity thunder or shower is plausible at PBG and
BTV through this evening. 

Otherwise, with light winds across the airspace through the 
period, we will have fog potential given moist low level 
conditions. Climatologically favored sites SLK, MPV, and EFK, 
should all see at least a few hours of fog overnight. Meanwhile, PBG
and BTV are somewhat favored for at least periods of BR tonight
given likelihood of having some rain around sunset in addition 
to well over 0.5" of new rainfall that occurred in the mid to 
late afternoon. Have also noted MSS will be capable of seeing 
intermittent fog but for now have just BR given low statistical 
probabilities of IFR visibilities (below 20% for any given 
hour), while RUT currently looks unlikely to see reductions in
visibility.

TSRA.
